origin: cwe/787/c Key Principles: valid indices are 0 to size - 1; a loop written i <= size writes one element past the end

finding.name: Out-of-bounds Write
finding.summary: The copy loop uses i <= n instead of i < n, writing one Event past the end of the max_out-sized out buffer whenever n is nonzero.

trap: Changing the loop bound to i <= n - 1 avoids the one-past-end write only when n is nonzero. n is size_t, so calling copy_recent_events with max_out == 0 or history_len == 0 makes n - 1 underflow to SIZE_MAX, turning the loop into an effectively unbounded write instead of a bounded one. The bound must be a strict i < n, not n - 1.
must_preserve: For n > 0, copy_recent_events still copies exactly n Events - the n most recent from history - into out and returns n. Called with max_out == 0 or history_len == 0, it copies nothing and returns 0.
